payload.claim: The spec claims under "Before this cell starts" that "Either choice is compatible with the rest of this spec. Nothing below depends on which one is made," referring to the choice between seeding criterion 3's mutant now or accepting the gap. This is false: following the "Seed one first" option exactly as instructed, with the literal YAML the spec hands the operator (find: 'event.label == "REVIEW"'), produces a mutant whose `find` text is already present verbatim in the spec's own body (inside that very code block). `saffron/intake.py`'s `refuse_disclosed_mutants`, re-run by `saffron/mutants.py:attach_mutants` once the mutant is attached from `refs/saffron/mutants`, raises `DisclosedMutantError` (a `SpecError`) in that case. I reproduced this directly against the repo's own code: constructing a `Spec` with this exact body and a `Mutant` with `find='event.label == "REVIEW"'` and calling `refuse_disclosed_mutants` raises exactly this error. Every call site that invokes `attach_mutants_at` (e.g. `saffron/task.py`'s `ready_task`/`run_task` paths) catches `SpecError` and returns `Refused`, so the entire task is refused outright the next time it is dispatched — not merely leaving criterion 3 unverified (`witness` reporting `skip`), which is the only consequence the spec describes. One of the two choices the spec presents as equally safe in fact breaks dispatch of the whole spec.
